facts.statement: Guemesia ochoai is the only known species in the genus, represented by a nearly complete braincase.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Guemesia ochoai, known from a nearly complete braincase.

facts.statement: Guemesia is considered one of the smallest abelisaurid dinosaurs known to science.
facts.quote: It is one of the smallest abelisaurids currently known.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as IBIGEO-P 103, consists of a small, nearly complete braincase.
facts.quote: The holotype of Guemesia, IBIGEO-P 103, is a small, nearly complete braincase.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in the Amblayo Valley within the Los Blanquitos Formation of Salta Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: It was found in the Los Blanquitos Formation, in the Amblayo Valley of Salta Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The species was formally described in 2022 by the research team led by Agnolín.
facts.quote: The specimen was described in 2022 by Agnolín et al.

facts.statement: The skull roof of Guemesia is highly ornamented, a feature similar to other abelisaurids.
facts.quote: esta presenta un techo craneal muy ornamentado similar al de otros abelisaurios.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the military leader Martín Miguel de Güemes, while the species name honors technician Javier Ochoa.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico “Guemesia” fue puesto en honor al gobernador y líder militar Martín Miguel de Güemes, mientras que su epíteto específico “ochoai” fue puesto en honor al técnico del Museo Regional Florentino Ameghino, Javier Ochoa.

facts.statement: Guemesia lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, approximately 84 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico hace aproximadamente entre 84 a 71 millones de años, durante el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Taxonomically, Guemesia is classified as a derived abelisaurid belonging to the clade Brachyrostra.
facts.quote: Agnolín et al. place Guemesia as a derived abelisaurid within the clade Brachyrostra.

facts.statement: The same formation containing Guemesia fossils also yields remains of the theropod Unquillosaurus and potential titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The controversial tetanuran theropod Unquillosaurus is also known from this formation, as well as fossils of what may belong to a species of Titanosaurus.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Guemesia spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Guemesia represents the first abelisaurid dinosaur discovered in this specific region of Argentina.
rejected.quote: ...and the first dinosaur of its kind known from the area.
